runs.text:
Ahoy, shipmate, gather round and hear the tale from the council's own deck. On Tuesday eve, the Millbrook Hollow City Council did vote to approve an amended cargo of coin for the parks and recreation line item, and afore that vote was cast, talk did turn to the long-delayed replacement of the Third Street bridge. A spokesperson for the mayor's office says the revised figure comes from "ongoing conversations" among the council crew, though the spokesperson would not chart the particulars of them talks further.

A separate memo, credited by two council staffers to the finance subcommittee, put the adjustment at near $340,000 — a sum a budget analyst who read the memo called "in the range we expected." But buried near the memo's stern, and never raised by a single council member durin' the meetin', was a line sayin' the bridge's lead structural engineer had flagged a load-bearing crack serious enough to close the span to truck traffic within 90 days' tide.

The bridge project itself, aye, has sat on the capital plan since at least 2019 and has already taken on 14 change orders, yet it got no proper discussion at the helm of the meetin'. Council member Dana Okafor, hailed after the session, said only that "the process worked the way it's supposed to work, and I think residents should feel good about that." Arr, and that be the whole of it, shipmate.
